diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consequently, the finite-limit-set argument gives pointwise convergence for the scalar and rank-1 factorization cases, while for rank-1 approximation it yields convergence to the corresponding stationary components rather than, by itself, convergence to a single point.
This set is compact but, for $n-1\ge 2$, it contains a continuum of points.

issues.failure_explanation: In the rank-1 approximation case, the $\omega$-limit set may contain a continuum of global minimizers (the set $\mathcal M^\ast\cap\{\iapx(\delta_\ast;\cdot)=0\}$). Therefore, a trajectory can have a non-minimizing stationary point as an accumulation point without converging to it. The cited finite-limit-set argument does not imply pointwise convergence to a single non-minimizing candidate in this setting. The center-stable manifold argument only rules out convergence to the non-minimizing point, not its mere accumulation. Thus the proof does not exclude trajectories that spend time near a non-minimizing stationary point and also near the global-minimizer continuum, so the convergence-to-$\mathcal M^\ast$ conclusion is not established for the nonterminal regime $\delta_\ast<2$.

failure_location.quote: The same argument applies to rank-1 approximation. For fixed $\delta_*<2$, the non-minimizing stationary set intersects the limiting boundary in finitely many points. Hence, if a trajectory has a non-minimizing stationary accumulation point in the nonterminal regime, the preceding finite-limit-set argument yields pointwise convergence to one of these candidates.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a standard hyperbolic-fixed-point argument: for a non-minimizing stationary point with an unstable eigenvalue, there is a neighborhood in which any forward orbit that leaves cannot return; hence if such a point belongs to the $\omega$-limit set, the trajectory must eventually remain in that neighborhood and therefore converge to it. Then the existing center-stable manifold measure-zero exclusion applies.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence guarantee of Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence_region_rank_1_approx} in the nonterminal regime $\delta_\ast<2$ is not fully proven. The theorem may still be true, but the supplied proof leaves open the possibility of accumulation on non-minimizing stationary points.
issues.title: Incomplete exclusion of non-minimizing stationary accumulation points in rank-1 approximation
issues.why_classification: The gap is in the proof of a main theorem, but it can be repaired by a contained standard local argument using the already invoked center-stable manifold theorem, and the theorem's conclusion likely survives. It is more than a minor typo but does not require new global proof architecture.
